claims: Same car, same 7.5 cm bump height; a 0.9 m bump gives a higher peak body acceleration than a 3.7 m hump at 10, 20 and 30 km/h in a quarter-car simulation with assumed values (not calibrated, not a safety statement). X-ray reveal view: translucent body with a spring and a damper per wheel following the simulation.
